requirements.requirement: Define sequential combination of the size-T block partial dot products.
requirements.evidence: padded zero-extends the original inputs; roundedProduct applies one multiplication error to each product. blockPartial sequentially accumulates exactly T padded products. computedDot sequentially accumulates B=ceil(n/T) such partials. sequentialSum takes the first entry directly and applies an addition error at each subsequent entry. This is the specified algorithm under the standard relative-error model; a hardware rounding implementation is not required.

requirements.requirement: Prove the stated two backward-error representations with gamma(T + ceil(n/T) - 1).
requirements.evidence: The final target explicitly gives computedDot=sum (x+Delta x)*y and computedDot=sum x*(y+Delta y), together with both bounds for every i:Fin n. For nonempty inputs K=errorIndex(n,T)=T+ceil(n/T)-1, and gamma(K,u)=K*u/(1-K*u). One multiplication, at most T-1 block additions and B-1 reduction additions affect each term. Empty inputs give empty sums and vacuous coordinate bounds.
